The test image shows a **dry, mature soybean stem** with numerous small black specks/fruiting bodies on the surface. The stem is grayish-tan colored. This narrows to **stem** classes.

Top candidates based on symptoms:
- **Anthracnose** - black acervuli with setae on stems
- **Charcoal_Rot** - microsclerotia giving charcoal-sprinkled appearance
- **White_Mold** - but no white fluffy growth visible

Let me view reference images, one at a time, starting with top candidates.
Anthracnose stem reference shows dark lesions with black specks on dry stems. Similar pattern to test image. Now let me check Charcoal_Rot.
Charcoal rot shows gray stem with peeling epidermis, different texture from the test image. Let me check Charcoal_Rot stem #2 for comparison.
This charcoal rot reference is very similar to the test image - small black specks (microsclerotia) scattered on a gray stem. Strong match. Let me continue checking other stem diseases.
White Mold shows bleached stem with fluffy white mycelium - very different from test image. Let me check more classes.
Rhizoctonia shows sunken lesions at the soil line on green seedlings - completely different from the test image. Let me check Phytophthora and Tobacco_Streak_Virus.
Phytophthora shows dark brown stem discoloration on living plants - not matching. Let me check Tobacco_Streak_Virus stem.

TSV shows green stem with node lesion - not matching. I have 1 view left. Let me compare the second Anthracnose stem reference more closely since Anthracnose and Charcoal_Rot are my top two candidates.

All 8 reference views used. Here's my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Dry, mature soybean stem
- Grayish-tan surface with numerous tiny black specks scattered densely across it
- "Charcoal-sprinkled" appearance
- Stem hairs visible

**Comparison:**
- **Charcoal_Rot** (Soybean_Dise_49.jpg) was the closest match: same pattern of tiny black microsclerotia densely scattered beneath the epidermis on a gray stem, giving the characteristic charcoal-sprinkled appearance.
- **Anthracnose** showed larger, more discrete black fruiting bodies (acervuli), not the fine speckling seen in the test image.
- White_Mold, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora, and TSV were clearly different (wrong growth stage, wrong symptom type).

The diagnostic feature is the numerous tiny black microsclerotia giving the "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance on the lower stem/taproot, which is the hallmark of Charcoal Rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*).
